domain: development approval / first-instance development application (DA) decisions, South Australia statewide register
prediction_question: OPEN between two candidate labels, to be fixed by the decision-date probe (next_action 1-2). Both share the same population (DAs lodged through the SA planning portal from 31/07/2020) and the same prediction instant (lodgement). Candidate A (preferred, higher utility): will this application be decided within the statutory timeframe applicable to its assessment pathway under the Planning, Development and Infrastructure Act 2016 - a per-application version of the statutory-timeframe KPI that SA/Vic/NSW report only as aggregate percentages. Candidate B: will the decision be a refusal (status in {Refused, Rejected}), with Withdrawn/Lapsed/Cancelled censored rather than negative. Prospective user: an applicant or their planning professional at/before lodgement, and councils forecasting assessment workload; a useful prediction supports pre-lodgement advice and resource allocation.
prediction_time: At lodgement of the application. Features displayed by the register that are documented at that instant: description (free text, e.g. 'Commercial', 'Verandah', 'Outbuilding (domestic storage shed)'), Assessment Pathway (e.g. 'Accepted'), Elements (e.g. 'Internal fitout', Demolition/Land division/Telecom codes DM/LD/TF/TA/RDT), Council area, Decision authority type (Assessment Manager / Assessment Panel / Council / DAC / Governor / Independent Assessor / Minister / SCAP / State Planning Commission), Act (DEV/PDI), applicant name, property address and title. Post-lodgement fields to exclude from features: status, decision, decision date, notification outcome, and any post-hoc reclassification. Two timing questions remain unresolved: (1) whether the displayed Assessment Pathway/category is exactly the value assigned at lodgement or a later-revised value (needs the PDI Act guidance pages); (2) no decision DATE has yet been observed on a detail page (only the decision TYPE on the Assessment tab), which blocks candidate A's latency label. The register is a current-state service: it showed applications lodged 05/11/2026 by the 06/11/2026 ~03:55Z fetch, and historical vintages are not archived, so a task built from it is retrospective with an explicit as-of assumption; decisions may also change after the fact (status vocabulary contains 'Decision Under Appeal', 'Lapsed').
target_definition: OPEN - pending the decision-date probe. Candidate A: binary label 1 = decision made more than the PDI Act statutory timeframe (working days, per pathway/category, clock-stop rules documented in the PDI (General) Regulations 2017 - rules not yet extracted; a published example decision is needed as a known-event fixture). Source columns: lodged date + decision date + pathway, decision date NOT YET CONFIRMED displayed per application. Candidate B: binary label 1 = decision status in {Refused, Rejected} (statuses documented in the register's own vocabulary: 'Refused' orange, 'This was refused.'; 'Rejected' orange, 'This was rejected.'); 0 = granted/approved; Withdrawn ('the applicant has withdrawn this application from assessment and no decision may be made'), Lapsed, Cancelled and still-Under-Assessment rows are censored and excluded from the label population - they are not negatives. Label source columns are excludable from shipped features.

sources.name: PlanSA Development Application Register (live search application)
sources.api: No documented public API. Working channels probed 2026-11-06: (1) server-rendered HTML search form (GET after form requestSubmit; direct URL navigation with only query params does NOT trigger the search); (2) bootstrap-table AJAX rendering of results; (3) CSV export endpoint https://plan.sa.gov.au/development_application_register/assets/daregisterCSV?payload=<btoa(JSON)> where JSON = {ActionType:'csv', Config:'public_register', DataObject:'PublicRegisterCSV', Params:<serialized form fields>, SortExpression, RecordNumber} - read from the page's own bundle public-register.min.js?v=0.15.5 (554,758 bytes); a synthetic payload fetch from page context failed ('TypeError: Failed to fetch'), so construction must replicate the page's exact handler. Plain HTTP clients (curl) get HTTP 403 from the site WAF - the supported browser session is required, same posture as candidates/fenz-incident-data.
sources.access: Anonymous, no login. Register states: 'allows you to search, track, and access publicly available information about development applications lodged in South Australia'; applications lodged before 31 July 2020 may sit in legacy council registers instead. Search filters measured: Status (All/Under Assessment/Decision Made/Lapsed/Withdrawn/Cancelled), Decision authority (9 values), Council area (all SA councils), Lodged date from/to (dd/mm/yyyy), Act (DEV/PDI), Applicant, street/suburb, application number/ID, title vol/fol, Elements, sort (LodgedNew/LodgedOld/AppId), perpage 25/50/100, page.

split_strategy: OPEN - per-year counts not yet measured in-session (date-window searches settle in 30-90 s in the browser and one 2021-window query did not settle within 75 s; per-year counts are a worker-side probe via Status-filtered searches or the CSV export). Population evidence so far: 299,858 DAs matched by the default search (2026-11-06); 260,174 with Status=Decision Made; 17,733 lodged 01/01/2026-06/11/2026. Rough intended design once counts exist: time-ordered windows by lodgement year (e.g. train 2020H2-2022, eval 2023-2024, holdout 2025-2026-to-date) with the label population restricted to decided applications; positives are expected to cluster by council and season (Christmas lodgement/decision lull), so record clustered counts (council-week) before claiming independence.

measurements.register_totals_2026_11_06: Read from the register's own result-count text in the supported browser session (UTC timestamps approximate, page clock 2026-11-06 03:30-04:15Z): default search 'We've found 299,858 development applications'; Status=Decision Made 260,174 (86.8% of all); Under Assessment 27,083; Lapsed 338; Withdrawn 10,538; Cancelled 1,725 (sum 299,858, consistent). Lodged 01/01/2026-06/11/2026: 17,733 (roughly 2,100/month, so a full lodgement year is on the order of 20k rows). Counts are the publisher's own displayed totals, not locally derived.
measurements.detail_schema_2026_11_06: Sample application 26037018 (192 THE PARADE NORWOOD SA 5067, lodged 5 November 2026, fetched 2026-11-06): Application summary tab shows Application ID, Lodged date, Application number ('N/A' for this one), Applicants, Assessment Pathway 'Accepted', Elements 'Internal fitout', Council area 'Norwood Payneham and St Peters', Title 'CT 5613/456 F139146 AL66', Public Notification 'Not applicable', status pill 'DECISION MADE'. Assessment tab shows per-consent decisions: 'This application requires Building Consent / Development Approval - Planning, Building' both 'Granted'. NO decision date displayed on this sample (decided within ~1 day; date-only display, so decision latency is measured to the day at best). List columns: Reference number, Applicant, Property address, Description, Lodged.
measurements.status_vocabulary_2026_11_06: Extracted from the register's own bundle public-register.min.js (PRstatusObj, verbatim descriptions): Lodged 'The application has been formally lodged by the applicant and is ready for assessment.'; Under Assessment '...awaiting decision.'; Approved 'The is approved.'; Decision Made 'Assessment of this application has completed and a decision has been made.'; Granted 'The is granted.'; Decision Under Appeal 'The decision made on the application by the relevant authority is being appealed in court, and may be upheld or overturned.'; Cancelled 'The was cancelled.'; Withdrawn 'The applicant has withdrawn this application from assessment and no decision may be made.'; Refused 'This was refused.'; Rejected 'This was rejected.'; Lapsed 'The decision made on this application has lapsed and is no longer valid.' The coarse search filter offers only Under Assessment/Decision Made/Lapsed/Withdrawn/Cancelled; Granted/Refused/Rejected/Approved/Decision Under Appeal are detail-level statuses.
measurements.access_cost_2026_11_06: plan.sa.gov.au returns 403 to plain curl (WAF) - supported browser required. In-session timings: Status-only search settles ~3-8 s; date-window searches settle 30-90 s (2026 window ~25-30 s; a 2021 window did not settle within 75 s); results render via bootstrap-table AJAX after the count text. perpage max 100 rows/page => ~3,000 pages for the full register, or windowed CSV exports via the payload endpoint (row cap unmeasured - the in-page click of 'Download .CSV of results' did not deliver a file to the browser workspace in-session; the payload recipe is recorded in sources[0].api).
measurements.au_comparator_registers_2026_11_06: data.gov.au catalogue sweep for DA/consent registers (anonymous package_search, scripts retained in probe/): City of Adelaide 'Current Development Applications' cc-by but ceased updating 2021-03-19 (dead); City of Playford per-year CSV DA register (2013 onward, cc-by, statutory Regulation 98 register - viable small fallback); ACT ACTGOV completed/active DAs via ACTmapi ArcGIS Hub (licence 'Other' - unverified); Moreton Bay QLD DAs via ArcGIS Hub (licence 'Other', weekly updates since 2016-02-01 - unverified); Victorian 'Building Permit Activity Data' per-year XLSB 2009-2026 (Building and Plumbing Commission, cc-by, >40 fields per permit, but permits issued with no decision-outcome field - carries no target). PlanSA is the only live statewide register with per-application decision statuses under a class-A licence.
measurements.nz_coverage_2026_11_06: Per this tick's regional focus: data.govt.nz catalogue is bot-walled for plain HTTP (Imperva, 'Pardon Our Interruption') but opens in the supported browser. Search 'resource consents' returned 327 datasets, dominated by regional council GIS layers (Horizons 91, Environment Canterbury 86, Otago RC 33, ...), formats HTML 319 / ArcGIS REST 282 / CSV 275, licence facets showing ~79 CC-licensed vs 9 'Other licensing'. NZ council resource-consent registers are activity permits (discharges, water takes) - a different population from first-instance development decisions, and licence verification per publisher would be required before any probe. No NZ candidate opened this tick; existing NZ candidates fenz-incident-data and nz-ea-wholesale-price-exceedance remain with their owners.
measurements.prior_art_scan_2026_11_06: Task-level prior art search (web, 2026-11-06): (1) ConfidentPlanner github.com/athuler/ConfidentPlanner - London planning approval-likelihood tool on the GLA London Planning Datahub (OGL v3), logistic regression + TF-IDF description embedding, AUC ~0.73, trained 2022-26; a tool with a trained model, NOT a published benchmark with splits/scored contract, and a different jurisdiction/decision system. (2) Lin et al. 2025, Sage J. Urban Planning 'Transforming urban planning through machine learning' - classifies Australian planning applications into development categories from description text (DeBERTa-v3 F1 0.944); text classification, not decision prediction; data available 'on reasonable request', not published ML-ready. (3) Aggregate accountability reporting only: Victoria reports '66% of all applications were processed within the statutory timeframes in 2023-24 (84 days median)'; NSW publishes council league tables of DA timeframes; RBA/Productivity-Commission 2025 housing-construction-productivity paper documents statutory-timeframe regimes per state (incl. SA) - all aggregate, none per-application, none a prediction task. Nearest family members in our own portfolio: pins-planning-appeal-outcome (GB, appeals of refused applications - different instant and population) and tc-gv-licence-application-outcome (operator licensing). No ML-ready per-application DA decision/latency benchmark with splits found anywhere; the statutory-timeframe compliance target in particular has no published predictor at all.
measurements.worked_example_2026_11_06: Dated example (all dates Australia/Adelaide, ACDT UTC+10:30; register displays dates only, so instants are day-granular): application 26037018, 192 The Parade Norwood SA 5067. Feature event window: everything up to lodgement on 05/11/2026 - description 'Commercial' (internal fitout), applicant Jones Lang LaSalle, Assessment Pathway 'Accepted', elements 'Internal fitout', council 'Norwood Payneham and St Peters'. First availability: present in the register search results when fetched 06/11/2026 ~03:55Z, i.e. within one day of lodgement (publication latency bounded at ~1 day by this one observation, not proven generally). Eligibility cutoff: lodged via the portal on/after 31/07/2020 (PDI Act); DEV-Act rows exist for some authorities. Prediction instant: lodgement, 05/11/2026 (ACDT). Target start/end: the decision event; observed status 'DECISION MADE' with 'Development Approval - Planning, Building - Granted' by fetch time 06/11/2026 ~04:15Z, so this application's decision window closed within ~1 day of lodgement (Accepted pathway; not representative of notified/assessed pathways). For a forward framing the whole target window follows the prediction instant; for this retrospective example the decision had already occurred at fetch time.

next_action: Cheapest decisive probes, in order (all browser-first; no worker money needed for 1-2): (1) DECISION-DATE probe - open 3-5 Decision-Made applications lodged 2020-2022 with Decision authority 'Council' and 'Assessment Panel' (Status=Decision Made search, then per-application Assessment tabs) and record whether any decision/consent date is displayed; this decides candidate A (statutory-timeframe latency) vs candidate B (refusal). (2) CSV probe - trigger 'Download .CSV of results' through the page's own handler on a Status=Decision Made search and inspect the exported columns and row cap (payload recipe recorded in sources[0].api); if the CSV carries decision date/status, per-year counts and refusal base rates become cheap. (3) If neither shows decision dates, a bounded worker aggregate probe (perpage=100 page walk, Status-filtered) to count Decision-Made by lodgement year and refusal prevalence, with measured request cost. (4) Extract the PDI Act 2016 statutory-timeframe rules per pathway/category from the Planning, Development and Infrastructure (General) Regulations 2017 and PlanSA guidance, and pin one published late decision as a known-event fixture. (5) Fix the target, then record the novelty verdict via scripts/check-novelty.py (ours: first-instance statewide SA decision/latency prediction with an explicit lodgement-time contract; theirs: ConfidentPlanner London tool, aggregate league tables, Lin et al. text classification). Verdict target: ready only after 1-4 are recorded; the licence (class A) and access contracts are already evidenced.
